Meeting header:

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery for Launchpad Labs evaluating Redwood for initial PLG/self-serve API onramp. Discussed free credits, time-to-first-request, hosted vs dedicated options for pilot, security needs (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and next steps to get a sandbox up and running.

Topics: quickstart flow, credentialing, security docs, pilot metrics, cost/latency tradeoffs, demo follow-up

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Maya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Ethan Cole: Good, thanks. Ethan here, CTO. We've got about 35 minutes, so we want to focus on how fast we can get to first requests and what the pilot looks like.
[00:14] Priya Narang: Hi, Priya—lead on engineering. Main questions are around data separation and whether we can do everything via self-serve first.
[00:20] Rafael Ortiz: Rafael from infra. I'll be the person looking at network / VPC stuff.
[00:24] Maya Singh: Great. Quick agenda: we cover your goals, walk through the self-serve quickstart, credit allocation, and then high-level security. Jordan will follow with next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Lena Brooks: Yep, sounds fine.

[00:40] Jordan Park: To start, Ethan, can you give us the success criteria for the pilot—what would make Redwood a win for Launchpad?
[00:46] Ethan Cole: Sure. Three things: one, get a demo-able integration into our app within two weeks; two, maintain sub-250ms median generation latency for short-form prompts; three, predictable cost so we can estimate monthly run rate. If those are met, we'll look at dedicated capacity after the pilot.
[01:05] Jordan Park: That's helpful. Two weeks to first demo is reasonable with our PLG path. Maya, quick note on latency profiles?
[01:11] Maya Singh: Yep. For hosted API we typically see low variance on requests under 256 tokens; median around 120–180ms depending on model. If you need <100ms consistently, dedicated or local quantized variants can help — but that usually moves you to Reserved/Dedicated.
[01:28] Rafael Ortiz: When you say dedicated, do you mean fully isolated GPUs on our VPC or Redwood-managed dedicated pools? We have compliance folks who prefer customer VPC where we control keys.
[01:38] Maya Singh: Two flavors: Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra with data isolation at the tenant level; Redwood Private is deploy-in-your-VPC or on-prem where you control KMS/HSM. For early pilot, most customers start hosted to move fastest and then evaluate Private if they need strict key control or on-prem.
[01:55] Priya Narang: Okay. For the pilot we want hosted if the data isn't PII, but we'd need to prove data handling — audit logs, retention periods. Do you have SOC 2 and an audit-ready log schema?
[02:06] Maya Singh: Yes — we have SOC 2 Type II and can provide the summary and the audit log formats. I'll attach those docs. Our hosted logs include per-request metadata, model, tokens used, timing, and a request id for tracing.
[02:19] Ethan Cole: Good. What about encryption? We want to use our KMS for keys; is that possible with hosted?
[02:24] Jordan Park: Hosted typically uses Redwood-managed keys, but we support customer KMS in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we provide TLS in transit and encryption at rest; if customer-managed keys are a hard req, we usually do Private.
[02:36] Rafael Ortiz: Understood. For this initial pilot we can use hosted but will flag the KMS requirement for later.

[02:42] Lena Brooks: How do free credits work? Are they tied to a single account, and do they expire?
[02:47] Jordan Park: We give a one-time credit pool for pilots — it shows up on your account as promo credits, one-time expiration of 90 days by default. We can tailor that window if procurement needs a different cadence. The credits apply to API usage (tokens + embeddings) but don't cover Dedicated monthly commits.
[03:02] Priya Narang: If we hit the credits quickly during a spike, is there throttling or rate limiting? We don't want surprises.
[03:08] Maya Singh: Good question. We set soft rate limits for new accounts, and we can bump them for pilots. We also provide per-api-key quotas so you can isolate dev vs prod traffic. We'll document recommended thresholds for your expected concurrency.

[03:25] Ethan Cole: Walk us through the actual flow to get our first token. What do devs need to do?
[03:30] Jordan Park: Minimal. Sign up -> create API key -> run sample curl or SDK snippet. We have a quickstart repo with examples in Node/Python and a Postman collection. Typical dev can be making requests in under an hour if they have no internal network blocks.
[03:45] Maya Singh: I'll call out two practical tips: 1) use the SDK to manage streaming responses and chunking for better UX; 2) set a prefix cache if you're doing repeated system prompts to save tokens. We'll send a sample that shows both.

[03:58] Rafael Ortiz: Are there specific egress IPs we need to allow for outbound to the hosted API?
[04:02] Maya Singh: Yes, we have a published IP range for our hosted endpoints and also recommend allowing SNI for TLS. For initial dev you can use open egress, but for locked-down environments we provide the ranges and certificate thumbprints.

[04:15] Lena Brooks: On the product side, our PM wants to track regression in quality — do you integrate with evaluation hooks or do we need to run separate tests?
[04:23] Maya Singh: Redwood Optimize has features for quality monitoring; for a pilot we recommend a small eval harness you can run on our hosted model. We'll include a sample eval set and an automated script to compare generations across model versions.

[04:38] Ethan Cole: Pricing: can you ballpark cost for a pilot doing ~200k tokens/week and occasional embeddings?
[04:46] Jordan Park: Rough ballpark: hosted model mid-tier might be $X per 1k tokens, so 200k tokens/week is in the low hundreds per week; embeddings are priced separately per 1k vectors. I'll put exact numbers in the follow-up email since pricing tiers vary by model and quantization.
[05:00] Priya Narang: We care about predictable spend — any tips to cap costs?
[05:04] Maya Singh: Set per-key quotas, use smaller context windows, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and pick a quantized model variant for generation. We'll share a recommended config for your workload.

[05:18] Ethan Cole: Another technical question — KV cache you mentioned earlier, how does that behave for conversational state when we use streaming?
[05:24] Maya Singh: The runtime maintains a KV cache per session. For streaming we stream tokens as they're generated and the cache is updated behind the scenes. There are limits for total context; we can advise on truncation strategies. Sometimes the transcripting engine mislabels KV as "K-V cash" in our docs, ha.
[05:40] Jordan Park: (laugh) we've seen that in generated docs too.

[05:44] Rafael Ortiz: For Dedicated later, if we reserve capacity, can we pin model versions? We worry about changes mid-flight.
[05:50] Maya Singh: Yes. You can pin to model version and we support staged rollouts. There's a rollback hook and canary routing so you can test without traffic disruption.

[06:03] Lena Brooks: Any gotchas when switching from hosted to dedicated or private mid-pilot?
[06:08] Maya Singh: Main things are key management and network connectivity. Model weights are compatible, but if you move to Private and want on-prem, there's a deployment window for infra validation. Most customers do a hosted pilot then plan a 2–4 week migration/validation for Private.

[06:25] Ethan Cole: Let's talk timeline — we want to be demoable in two weeks. What would you need from us?
[06:31] Jordan Park: For a two-week path: 1) sign up and accept TOS; 2) share the dev list of endpoints and a sample prompt; 3) Redwood provisions credits and increases dev quotas; 4) we schedule a 1-hour sandbox walkthrough. If we get those items within 48 hours, two-week push is doable.
[06:48] Priya Narang: I'll be sending the sample prompts and the endpoints. Any special formatting?
[06:52] Maya Singh: JSON array with example context + target output is perfect. We'll use that to create a quick eval to demonstrate parity.

[06:59] Jordan Park: On the procurement side — any blockers we should be aware of?
[07:03] Ethan Cole: Mostly approvals for external services and our security team review. Procurement wants standard SLA language; we might need to escalate to legal if we go to Dedicated.
[07:12] Jordan Park: Understood — we can share standard SLA and enterprise terms. For pilots we typically accept the platform's standard terms.

[07:19] Lena Brooks: Who is our main Redwood contact for the walkthrough?
[07:22] Jordan Park: That would be me for coordination and Maya for technical. We'll both be there.

[07:27] (short silence)

[07:30] Maya Singh: Small aside — we usually recommend people test both a small embedding workload and one gen endpoint during pilot to validate both pricing and latency assumptions. We'll include an example dashboard template you can plug in.

[07:44] Rafael Ortiz: One more infra detail — what's the retention window for logs and can we toggle retention to shorter periods?
[07:50] Maya Singh: Hosted default is 90 days for access logs. For enterprise tiers you can request different retention policies. Private gives you full control. We'll include retention options in the security doc.

[08:02] Ethan Cole: Any references from similar customers? We liked the Novaquill note in your materials — anything in fintech/regulated spaces?
[08:09] Jordan Park: We have anonymized case studies — I'll share two that map to regulated teams who started on hosted then moved to Dedicated.

[08:16] Priya Narang: If we sign up and start the quickstart, how do we separate dev vs prod keys and rotate keys?
[08:22] Maya Singh: Use multiple API keys with different scopes/quotas; keys can be rotated via the console/API and we enforce immediate invalidation on rotation. We'll show the CLI snippet.

[08:33] Jordan Park: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll list them and Maya will confirm docs: 1) Jordan sends quickstart and credits details, 2) Maya attaches SOC2 + network ranges + SDK examples, 3) Launchpad to share sample prompts + throughput targets, 4) schedule sandbox walkthrough.

[08:50] Ethan Cole: Sounds good. One last question — do you support role-based access in the Console for our team?
[08:55] Maya Singh: Yes, RBAC with teams and invite flows; SSO via SAML is supported on enterprise plans but we can demo invite flows for the pilot.

[09:03] Lena Brooks: Great. If you can send the docs today we'll target an internal kickoff Friday.
[09:08] Jordan Park: Will do. Anything else?
[09:11] (brief cross-talk)

[09:15] Priya Narang: No, that's it. Thanks both.

[09:19] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and schedule the sandbox session.

[09:24] (meeting ends)
